name: deploy_runbook
description: Manage Custom Runbook lifecycle: register (store as DRAFT) or deploy (DRAFT→DEPLOYED). Custom runbooks are named ASR-Custom-{standard}_{version}_{control}. On deploy, ASR provisions a scoped remediation role in each member account using the existing cross-account trust chain (API Lambda → Orchestrator Admin Role → Orchestrator Member Role). The role's trust policy allows the Orchestrator Member Role and ssm.amazonaws.com to assume it. The role gets two inline policies: a base policy (SSM parameters, PassRole, StartAutomationExecution) and a remediation policy with the required_iam_actions you provide. Use specific actions (e.g. 's3:PutBucketEncryption') not wildcards ('s3:*').

__authorizationHeader.description: Internal: injected by gateway interceptor. Do not set manually.

name: drift_detection
description: Developer tool: push a runbook YAML to a test account's SSM, execute it against a finding, or check execution status. Use 'push' to create/update the SSM Automation document, 'execute' to run it against a Security Hub finding, 'status' to check results. After execution, poll 'status' until the execution reaches a terminal state, then use get_finding_history or findings to confirm Security Hub's compliance state once it re-evaluates the resource. 'push' and 'execute' are disabled unless the deployment enables the developer fast-loop.

__authorizationHeader.description: Internal: injected by gateway interceptor. Do not set manually.

name: test_remediation_script
description: Fast inner-loop test for a candidate Python remediation script. Creates a transient SSM Automation document with aws:executeScript, runs it, returns per-step output, and deletes the document.

python_script.description: Inline Python source for the remediation handler. The handler must return a dict — a list or scalar return value fails with an opaque output-selector error.

input_payload.description: Dict passed to the handler as its event parameter.

handler.description: Python handler function name. Defaults to "handler".

runtime.description: Python runtime for aws:executeScript. Defaults to python3.11.

control_id.description: Optional control ID used to name the transient document.

automation_assume_role.description: IAM role ARN SSM assumes when executing the script. There is no default and nothing injects it, not even the deployed MCP server: always pass it, or the call is rejected. The role must be in this server's account, at the root IAM path (no `role/<path>/` segment), and its name must begin with "SO0111-Remediate-Custom-Test-" — that is the only role pattern the MCP server is allowed to iam:PassRole to SSM, and any other role ARN fails inside StartAutomationExecution. Optional in the schema only so the rejection can name the parameter.

timeout_seconds.description: Hard timeout for the test execution. Defaults to 300 seconds. Capped at 600 — the SSM aws:executeScript action this tool always builds does not run longer than that.

cleanup.description: Delete the transient SSM document after execution. Defaults to true.

document_name.description: Explicit document name to use; otherwise one is generated.

__authorizationHeader.description: Internal: injected by gateway interceptor. Do not set manually.

name: test_runbook_yaml
description: End-to-end test for a full SSM Automation runbook YAML. Registers a transient document, runs all mainSteps, reports per-step status and outputs, then deletes. Set skip_execution=true to only validate SSM accepts the schema. Pass runbook_id and version to record the outcome against a registered version, which is what makes it deployable — deploy_runbook refuses any version that has not passed here.

runbook_yaml.description: Full SSM Automation document content (YAML by default). Capped at 65536 — SSM's CreateDocument content quota — since this is registered as-is, with no wrapper around it.

input_parameters.description: Parameters passed to StartAutomationExecution. Non-string values are JSON-encoded automatically. For a registered-version test, AutomationAssumeRole is set to the bounded test role.

document_name.description: Explicit document name to use; otherwise one is generated.

document_format.description: Format of runbook_yaml. Defaults to YAML.

control_id.description: Optional control ID used to name the transient document.

runbook_id.description: Registered runbook this test belongs to (UUID, as returned by deploy_runbook register). Supply with `version` and `required_iam_actions` to provision its version-and-permission-set-scoped test role and record the outcome. Omit all three for a throwaway test run.

version.description: Registered version being tested. Required alongside `runbook_id` and `required_iam_actions`.

required_iam_actions.description: Exact IAM actions the registered runbook needs. Required with runbook_id/version. ASR provisions a bounded test role scoped to this version and permission set; deploy_runbook later requires the same set.

timeout_seconds.description: Hard timeout for the whole execution. Defaults to 600 seconds. This bounds the overall multi-step Automation execution, not a single step's own timeoutSeconds — a runbook using aws:waitForAwsResourceProperty or aws:runCommand can legitimately run well past the 600s cap that applies specifically to a single aws:executeScript step. Capped at 800s because this tool polls to completion inside the MCP Lambda: the poll budget is timeout_seconds + 30, and the Lambda is bounded at 900s by both Lambda and AgentCore synchronous-request limits, leaving the remainder for document create/delete. An Automation that genuinely needs longer cannot be observed synchronously and needs an async execute-then-poll path instead.

cleanup.description: Delete the transient SSM document after execution. Defaults to true.

skip_execution.description: If true, only register the document (to verify SSM accepts it) and then delete it. No execution is started.

__authorizationHeader.description: Internal: injected by gateway interceptor. Do not set manually.

name: update_controls
description: Bulk enable or disable auto-remediation for one or more controls, or apply/remove a filter across all of them. For `operation: "update"` pass `data`: the controls to write, each carrying its current `version` from list_controls. For `applyFilterToAll` / `removeFilterFromAll` pass `filterId` (from list_filters) instead of `data`. Entries are applied independently: an entry whose `version` is stale is rejected and the others are still written. HTTP 200 means every entry was applied; 207 means some were and lists the rest in `failedControlIds`; 409 means none were. `failedControlIds` also includes the ids in `rejectedControlIds` when present: those are controls served by a custom runbook, which cannot have automated remediation enabled and are refused identically on every retry — do not retry them. Refresh versions and retry only the failed ids that are not in `rejectedControlIds`.

data.description: For `update`: the controls to write, each carrying its current `version` from list_controls.

__authorizationHeader.description: Internal: injected by gateway interceptor. Do not set manually.
